Declaring: a command declaration may add `owns: [table.column, ...]` to its `command:` block; each entry names a table in that command's `writes` and a real column (case-insensitive, like SQLite), checked at write time and by `benmore check`. `deleted_at` and `updated_at` cannot be owned (written by generic DELETE / every UPDATE). The declaration takes effect as soon as the flow loads, bound or not: in an app with no mcp.yaml the command flow loads without a connector (it cannot run) and its owned columns are refused all the same, which is how an app without a connector keeps a column out of generic CRUD. Once mcp.yaml exists, every command flow must be bound in it (`connector_commands`).

Refusal: for every column owned by any command in the current runtime generation, generic auto-CRUD refuses a request that names it with 403 {"error":"field_owned_by_command","field":"table.column","command":"<name>","message":"this field can only be changed by its command"} (`field` repeats the request's spelling of the column): create, update, singleton upsert, batch create/update, streaming ingest (the whole stream), `/api/_transaction`, `POST /api/_groups/create` (org-table columns), the admin panel's create/update (they dispatch to generic CRUD; the panel's create form has no input for an owned column and its edit form shows the value read-only, so its forms never name one), the workflow transition route when the owned column is its state field, bulk import Mode A (create-time `columns` and the loader), and the native connector table update. Admin sessions are refused too: ownership is a write path, not a permission. NDJSON import fails the load on an owned key (unknown keys stay ignored).

Echo and create: an UPDATE that echoes the column's current stored value is a no-op and is allowed (a full-row form post) only when the caller can read that column (not hidden, not encrypted/masked, read access and scope allow it, row viewable), so the answer is never an equality oracle; an echo-only PATCH answers 200 `{"status":"updated"}` with nothing written; a changed value is refused, echoing NULL as an empty string counts as a change, and create, batch update and the native connector update refuse any owned key. Creating a row without naming the field is allowed and the DB default applies. A version revert restores every other column and leaves owned ones unchanged (`owned_fields_kept`).

Boundary: ownership constrains generic CRUD field writes only. Not blocked: other commands (no cross-command check), ordinary flows (`run: sql`), hooks, cron, flow operations such as `import_csv`, workflow timeout transitions, generic DELETE (soft delete writes `deleted_at` under delete access), operator SQL (`sql write:true`, seed/reset) and Mode B SQL restore. The command's own apply keeps its own checks: scopes, validators, workflow guards and hooks, and not the table's `access:` rule (`connector_hooks_effects`). Reload publishes the owned set with the commands, so removing the declaration or the command lifts the restriction.
